newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. Council raps Kabila on refugees in E. Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Council raps Kabila on refugees in E. Zaire.

text.p: The Security Council on Thursday joined Secretary-General Kofi Annan in harshly criticising Zairean rebels under Laurent Kabila for preventing aid from reaching up to 100,000 refugees and obstructing their return home to Rwanda.
The 15-member council at a formal meeting called "in the strongest terms" on Kabila's rebel movement "to ensure unrestricted and safe access by all humanitarian relief agencies."

It said in a statement it was concerned at the "obstruction of repatriation plans" for the refugees and said the rebels, known as the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo/Zaire, as well as the Rwandan government should cooperate with U.N. agencies "without delay."
In addition, the council said it was alarmed by reports of massacres in eastern Zaire and said the rebels should allow U.N. investigators to inspect certain sites.
Annan on Wednesday said he was "shocked and appalled at the inhumanity" of the rebels in obstructing aid to the refugees, saying they were, in effect, killing people through starvation.

"I do not think the international community can stand by as thousands of men and women and children are starved to death. You can kill by shooting or by starvation. Killing by starvation is what is going on," he said.
Most of the refugees were Rwandan Hutus who fled their country after the 1994 massacre of hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Tutsis and moderate Hutus by Hutu troops and militia.
Kabila's alliance, which threatens to topple the government of President Mobutu Sese Seko, favours Tutsis who have taken over Rwanda's government.

The council was meeting shortly after a U.N. team discovered up to 55,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees missing from the Kasese camp in the jungle of eastern Zaire and was blocked by rebels from a wider search.
The Hutus had arrived at Kasese and Biaro in mid-March after six months of trekking over volcanic rock and through thick bush and jungle in a vain attempt to flee the Tutsi-dominated rebels.
